# Testing Conventions

vitest everywhere; how it is invoked differs per workspace.

Per-workspace test commands, the test file layout convention, the root contract gates, and the
exact coverage floor numbers: reference `test-suites-and-coverage-gates`. Read it before running a
suite, adding a test file, or reacting to a coverage gate failure. Coverage floors are regression
guards, not targets -- never raise one to sit flush against the current number.

## Structure

- AAA: Arrange / Act / Assert, separated by blank lines.
- Descriptive test names: `it('rejects PKCE plain challenge', ...)`. State the scenario and the expectation. Never `it('works')`.
- One assertion theme per `it`. Share setup with `beforeEach`; never share mutable state across cases.

## Mandatory Coverage (Critical, Security-Sensitive Paths)

Every one of these has existing tests -- extend them, do not start a parallel suite.

- Protocol correctness: PKCE S256 enforcement, exact `redirect_uri` matching, refresh rotation plus family revocation on replay, the four WebAuthn checks, `jti` replay defense.
- Tenant isolation / privilege escalation: an org A context reaching an org B resource MUST assert 403 or 404 and MUST NOT leak existence. Anchors: `packages/db/src/__tests__/isolation.test.ts` (asserts the query layer injects the predicate) and `apps/server/worker/v1/__tests__/isolation.test.ts` (asserts the HTTP surface). See tenant-isolation rule.
- Password: Argon2id hash and verify, HIBP breach lookup, single-use reset tokens.
- Token: issuance and verification, expiry, near-real-time revocation through the Durable Object.
- Enumeration defense: opaque and uniform error responses, constant-time behavior.

## Focus on Boundaries and Negative Paths

- Failure and edge cases: empty input, oversized input, expiry, concurrency, cloned `sign_count`, clock skew.
- The valibot failure path for every untrusted input (see error-handling rule).

## Do Not Test

- Placeholders, pure types, framework boilerplate. Never write a meaningless test to move a coverage number.
- Third-party library behavior -- trust their own test suites.
